 Interim Black Stars coach Bjorkegren admits challenging circumstances ahead of AFCON qualifiers against Somalia  
 November 12, 2026 
 No Comments

 WhatsApp 
 By: Nana Karikari, Senior Global Affairs Correspondent  
 Ghana’s interim men’s national soccer coach, Kim Lars Bjorkegren, has admitted he faces unique challenges and a compressed preparation window ahead of Thursday’s crucial 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Somalia. 
 Sudden Transition in Leadership  
 Kim Lars Bjorkegren 
 Bjorkegren took the temporary job after veteran manager Carlos Queiroz resigned last month. The move marks a rapid shift for Bjorkegren, who also coaches the Black Queens, Ghana’s senior women’s national team. 
 Thursday’s match at the Sekondi Sports Stadium will be his first game managing a senior men’s side. The Swedish coach openly acknowledged the tight turnaround facing his technical staff. 
 ‘‘Yeah, of course there has been less preparation for me, but I am doing my best,’’ Bjorkegren said ahead of the match. 
 Building Squad Cohesion Quickly  
 To get up to speed with his roster, Bjorkegren traveled across Europe to scout players in person. He also spoke with nearly the entire squad by phone before camp opened in West Africa. 
 ‘‘I have been around a little bit, in Europe to watch some players. I have tried to connect with more or less all the players by phone, and now they are here in Ghana where we have had two training sessions, and we will have another one,’’ he explained. 
 High Stakes in Group C  
 The short runway leaves zero margin for error in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Ghana sits last in Group C after losing its opening two matches to Ivory Coast and The Gambia. Those defeats—a 2–0 loss in Bouaké and a 4–2 setback in Accra—left the four-time African champions without a single point. 
 To keep qualification hopes alive, the Black Stars must win both upcoming games against Somalia. Somalia also enters the doubleheader seeking its first Group C points after narrow losses to The Gambia and Ivory Coast. 
 Tactical Focus and Venue Logistics  
 Despite limited time on the pitch, Bjorkegren expressed confidence that his players will execute his game plan on Thursday. He noted that team meetings have helped bridge the tactical gap. 
 ‘‘There have been some meetings, of course, where we have discussed how we want to play, how we want to create chances, score goals and how we want to win this game,’’ Bjorkegren said. 
 Kickoff at Sekondi Sports Stadium is set for 3 p.m. local time on Thursday. Because Somalia currently lacks a stadium approved for senior international fixtures, both nations will remain at the same Ghanaian venue for Monday’s return leg. 
 Resonating Across Ghanaian and African Football Culture  
 The high-stakes doubleheader touches a nerve across the continent, where the Black Stars remain one of football’s most iconic symbols. Millions of supporters across West Africa and beyond are watching closely as the team looks to rebound from its recent continental setbacks. For Ghanaian fans packing the stands in Sekondi, these fixtures represent more than routine qualifiers—they are a critical first step toward restoring national pride and continental dominance ahead of the 2027 tournament co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. 
 Looking Beyond the Doubleheader  
 The next five days carry major consequences for both sides. Six points would revive Ghana’s qualifying campaign and stabilize a program still searching for a permanent head coach. For Somalia, spoiling Ghana’s plans in Sekondi would deliver a landmark result in Group C.
